registry.notes: COVERED — Exclusion validated 2026-04-06. Commitment as a psychological state — the deliberate binding of the will to a person, cause, or covenant — has no single Hebrew or Greek lexical anchor. The inner act of committing is expressed through the covenant (berith), faithfulness (emunah/chesed), and loyalty vocabulary. Commitment is the interior dimension of covenant: what makes a promise more than a statement of current intent. The absence of a discrete term reflects the biblical integration of volitional, relational, and covenantal categories rather than a programme gap. Covered by faithfulness (#60), loyalty (#104), covenant (#34). No further action required. Source: Session-A-v9-Empty-Words-Analysis-20260318.
registry.description: Commitment is the inner act of binding oneself to a person, a course of action, or a promise — giving one's word and staking one's reliability on it. The biblical vocabulary distributes this concept across the words for faithfulness, loyalty, and covenant-keeping rather than giving it a single term. Commitment is the interior dimension of covenant: what makes a promise more than a statement of current intent. [Covered by faithfulness (#60), loyalty (#104), covenant (#34).]
registry.inference_note: Commitment as a psychological state — the deliberate binding of the will to a person, cause, or covenant — is ABSENT as a single biblical term. The concept is expressed through covenant, vow, and dedication vocabulary.
